themes.theme: H1 2026 M&A hits all-time record on mega-deal concentration
themes.summary: Global M&A ~$2.7T for H1 2026 (+47% YoY, +88% vs H1 2024) per LSEG, with >50% of volume from deals >=$5b for the first time ever -- even as total deal count fell 10% YoY (20% in the US) to a post-2020 low. Global PE also up sharply: $583b (+54% YoY) across 5,729 deals. History (4 prior >$2T first-half years) suggests a pullback is likely to follow.

themes.theme: AI capital keeps flowing into infra, memory, and 'physical economy' training data
themes.summary: SK Hynix filed for a Nasdaq listing that could raise >$29b (HBM memory bottleneck for AI buildout); Baseten finalizing $1.5b at $11-13b; General Intuition (BFD) raised $320m at $2.3b to train AI on gaming video/inputs; Groq disclosed a $650m round as it pivots from chipmaker to inference neocloud (13 data centers, targeting 200MW by 2027).

themes.theme: SPAC market's 'second boom' matures into a going-public pipeline
themes.summary: 251 pre-deal SPACs hold ~$47b in capital plus 110 live deSPAC deals (SPACResearch.com); Chamath Palihapitiya candidly disavowed his own past SPAC incentive structure on The Axios Show. Concretely: Agility Robotics (humanoid robots, $2.5b implied) and Elroy Air (cargo drones, $800m pre-money) both agreed to go public via SPAC reverse mergers; Remix Therapeutics did the same via Passage Bio.

themes.theme: PE housing-ownership limits advance in the Senate
themes.summary: The bipartisan 21st Century Road to Housing Act (50 measures) heads to a Senate vote, capping large institutional (350+ home) purchases of single-family homes going forward -- though it exempts pre-existing holdings and PE-built homes, leaving Brookings' ~3% institutional-ownership estimate largely intact for now.

themes.theme: Large-cap healthcare/biotech M&A stayed hot but is down-weighted here
themes.summary: AbbVie/Apogee Therapeutics ($10.9b), Merck(Germany)/Bio-Techne ($11.4b), Thoreau/Ensemble ($12b), H.B. Fuller/Advanced Medical Solutions (£715m) and a wave of biotech VC rounds (Ollin $330m, Osanni $190m, Trase $107m) all landed this week -- see preferences.md down-weighting; noted briefly, not highlighted.

SK Hynix's giant Nasdaq listing, Advent International's ~$1.24b bid for nursing-care firm Japan Well-being, and Bain Capital/Blackstone advancing to round two on Fuji Media's real estate unit ($6.3b) all point to accelerating Japanese asset churn, alongside the ongoing Kakaku bidding war (documented in the following week's data).
